subject.title: fix(reply): strip leaked current-message scaffolding and (no output) placeholders

question: Should OpenClaw accept this shared reply-sanitizer and normalizer behavior as the canonical fix for the linked reply leak before merge?
rationale: The patch intentionally changes cross-channel message delivery semantics by stripping copied prompt scaffolding and suppressing bare `(no output)` replies; that is a maintainer merge-risk choice even though no concrete code defect was found.

options.title: Land after exact-head checks
options.body: Accept the scoped stripping/suppression semantics and merge once the current broad CI failures are cleared or triaged as unrelated.

options.title: Ask for live Telegram proof
options.body: Keep the code shape but request a short Telegram Desktop proof before merge if maintainers want visible channel evidence in addition to terminal production-function proof.

options.title: Rework the semantic boundary
options.body: Pause or close this PR if maintainers decide copied prompt scaffolding should be handled by a different owner boundary or narrower marker contract.

recommendation.title: Land after exact-head checks
recommendation.body: Accept the scoped stripping/suppression semantics and merge once the current broad CI failures are cleared or triaged as unrelated.
